record.paper_title: Collective Phenomena in the LiHoxY1−xF4 Quantum Ising Magnet: Recent Progress and Open Questions
record.original_question: Do sample shape and demagnetization effects influence whether a spin-glass phase exists in highly diluted LiHoxY1−xF4, even though such effects are expected not to determine the existence of the spin-glass phase?

evidence.quote: Sample shape and demagnetization effects should not affect the existence of the spin glass phase, but this should nevertheless be investigated.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the dipolar Ising magnet LiHo$_x$Y$_{1-x}$F$_4$, in which magnetic Ho$^{3+}$ ions are randomly substituted by non-magnetic Y$^{3+}$ ions at concentration $1-x$, and the remaining Ho$^{3+}$ ions carry effective Ising moments coupled predominantly through long-range, anisotropic magnetic dipole-dipole interactions. In the highly diluted regime (small $x$), the question of whether a thermodynamic spin-glass phase exists at low temperature is of central interest. Because dipolar interactions are long ranged, the magnetostatic energy of a finite sample depends on its shape, leading to demagnetization corrections that depend on the sample geometry.

Determine whether sample shape and the associated demagnetization effects can influence the existence (as opposed to merely the location or sharpness) of an equilibrium spin-glass phase transition in highly diluted LiHo$_x$Y$_{1-x}$F$_4$. Specifically, decide whether two macroscopic samples with the same Ho concentration $x \ll 1$ but different shapes (e.g. needle-like versus oblate) must exhibit the same answer to the question "is there a finite-temperature spin-glass phase?", or whether shape/demagnetization can change this answer.
artifact.status_search_result: Studies of dilute LiHo$_x$Y$_{1-x}$F$_4$ continue to debate whether a true spin-glass phase exists at small $x$ (with conflicting reports of glassy dynamics versus antiglass behavior at $x=0.045$, and reported transitions at other dilutions). No work appears to have decisively settled whether sample shape/demagnetization corrections can change the existence of the spin-glass phase; the issue remains an open experimental and theoretical question.

status_evidence.title: Evidence of spin glass dynamics in dilute LiHoxY1-xF4
status_evidence.snippet: ac susceptibility and specific heat measurements on dilute LiHoxY1−xF4 show glassy behavior with finite-temperature spin-glass transitions.
status_evidence.claim: The existence of a spin-glass phase in dilute LiHoxY1-xF4 is actively debated, with sample-dependent observations.

status_evidence.title: Quantum and classical glass transitions in LiHoxY1-xF4
status_evidence.snippet: Dynamical scaling suggests a spin-glass transition temperature of 43±2 mK at x=0.045.
status_evidence.claim: Reports of spin-glass transitions exist but interpretation depends on sample details.

status_evidence.title: Microscopics of Quantum Annealing in the Disordered Dipolar Ising Ferromagnet LiHoxY1-xF4
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (post-2020) work on the disordered dipolar Ising system continues to investigate phase structure.
status_evidence.claim: The phase structure question remains under active investigation, with no definitive resolution of shape/demagnetization influence on the spin-glass phase's existence.
